One common test is the cover-up test, where the doctor covers one eye and checks if your child can see the object in the other eye. Another test is the preferential eye patching test, where a patch is placed on one eye and the doctor checks if the child can see the object in the other eye. The doctor can also use a pinhole test, where the doctor places a pinhole over one eye and checks if the child can see the object in the other eye. The doctor can also use a visual acuity test, where the doctor checks how well your child can see at different distances.
